image_description: A close-up, slightly low-angle view of a beige audio cassette tape against a blue background. The cassette features two visible spools with dark magnetic tape wound around them. There is a paper label on the top half with stylized text and a strip of tape extending from the bottom spool area towards the right. The bottom edge shows the characteristic rectangular opening and small molded details.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object clearly exhibits the proportions of a standard cassette: wide and tall relative to its thin depth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flat rectangular prism with rounded corners.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall shape is a rectangle with visibly rounded corners, consistent with injection-molded plastic casings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Two circular holes revealing tape spools inside.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct circular windows are present, showing the internal spool mechanisms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Two spools of magnetic tape visible through circular holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark, wound material resembling magnetic tape is visible on the spools within the circular windows.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular opening at bottom exposing tape for player head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bottom edge features the standard wide rectangular slot used for tape access in players.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface has molded details screw holes tape guide slots and write-protect tabs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While there are some dark shapes near the bottom that might represent guide posts or screw holes, they lack the crisp, functional geometry of real molded plastic. They appear as vague dark blobs rather than precise mechanical features. No clear write-protect tab is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Casing transparent or opaque plastic typically black gray or clear.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The casing appears to be opaque beige/cream plastic, which is a valid color for cassettes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Label area on one face displaying track information artist and title.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a label area, but the text is gibberish/nonsensical symbols rather than legible track information, artist, or title. This fails the 'displaying information' criteria.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Visible internal spools through transparent casing.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The spools are visible through the designated windows.

artifact_observations.location: Top label area and bottom strip
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the label consists of nonsensical, alien-like characters and distorted Latin letters (e.g., 'I QDL', 'Moo'). The strip of tape extending out also has illegible writing on it. This is a classic AI generation failure in rendering text.

The small rectangular holes and posts along the bottom edge (meant for mechanism engagement) are misshapen, unevenly spaced, and lack the sharp edges of molded plastic. They look like melted or poorly formed voids.

A strip of what looks like tape or paper extends diagonally from the center/bottom area. It has text on it but doesn't connect logically to the spools in a physically accurate way (it seems to float or emerge from nowhere). The texture is overly smooth and plastic-like compared to real magnetic tape.
The teeth on the spools inside the windows are irregular and inconsistent in shape, lacking the uniform precision of manufactured plastic parts.

To check for boundary bleeding between the cassette and the background, and to verify the continuity of the plastic shell.
To assess the general realism and identify any subtle lighting or shading inconsistencies typical of AI generations.

focus_areas: Legibility and semantic correctness of text on labels
Geometric precision of molded plastic details (spool teeth, bottom slots)
Physical plausibility of the loose tape/paper strip
Edge sharpness between cassette and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text auditor's output. If the text is completely nonsensical, this is a major artifact for a 'cassette' which typically relies on legible labels for context. Also, verify if the 'melted' look of the bottom slots is a structural failure or just low resolution. The loose strip in the middle is suspicious—check if it defies physics.
